To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) a simple hash function is good enough for most applications and (2) a good hash function is a function with good randomness properties.

(a) the performance of simple hash functions in practice arises naturally from a combination (Renyi entropy of the data + randomness of the hash functions); (b) this performance is independent of the family of hash functions used; (c) the analysis for 2-universal families is tight; and (d) the analysis for O(1)-universal families can be improved to match the analysis for 3-universal families, but not for 2-universality.
the entropy in a stream of data can be exploited in order to achieve the best possible performance when using simple hashing schemes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental issue in hashing: how does the choice of hash function affect the performance of hashing?
the question of why simple hashing algorithms work so well in practice.
understanding the behavior of hashing in practice, and we show that it is possible to give a rigorous justification for the strong performance of 2-universal hashing in practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the entropy in the data stream is a key factor in determining the behavior of simple hashing algorithms, and that this entropy can be exploited to achieve the same strong guarantees as for truly random hashing.
, if the input data has sufficient entropy, then the performance of universal hash families is essentially the same (up to constant factors) as that for a truly random function.
the performance of universal hash families is as good as random hashing, as long as the data has a sufficient amount of entropy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the entropy in a stream of data can be exploited by a simple hash function, even if the hash function is not random, and that the resulting performance can be as good as that obtained by a truly random hash.
, if you are using a 2-univeral hash function to hash data that has a lot of entropy (i.e., is random), then it doesn't matter that you are using a universal hash function.
the entropy in the data stream can be exploited to make the performance of a universal hash function approach that of a truly random function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of universal hash families in practice can be explained by the fact that real data has entropy, and that the randomness in the hash function is sufficient to extract the entropy in the data.
the performance of simple hashing in practice can arise from the combination of the randomness from the hash function with the entropy from the data.

the entropy of a stream of data can be a powerful tool in the analysis of algorithms and data structures, and that the performance of hashing algorithms in practice can be explained and analyzed by combining the randomness of a hash function with the statistical properties of the data.
